synoptic.summary: The shortwave ridge over the Great Basin moves east on Sunday. Ahead of a weak, moisture-starved trough, flow from 185°–210° strengthens to 17–23 kt at 3,400–5,200 ft above the POM landings, which is a mixing-down risk. It also keeps the valley flow at 140°–160° all day, so no afternoon switch is forecast Sunday. The trough crosses Monday with a 7–16% shower chance and 3% thunder. Flow aloft drops below 10 kt, and the usual switch to 310°–340° arrives around 14:00. Ridging rebuilds Tuesday with very light flow aloft (≤10 kt below ~5,500 ft above landing), but the launch forecast keeps 170° all afternoon.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: The upstream shortwave ridge will move east on Sunday allowing southwesterly flow to overspread the forecast area in advance of an approaching shortwave trough. The resultant warming trend will push daytime temperatures back near climo Sunday. This progressive, moisture starved trough quickly translate across the region Monday, bringing a chance for mainly mountain showers with minimal accumulation.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport read 1018.5 mb at 16:54 local Saturday. That is up from 1016.6 mb at 07:54 and has held at 1018.1–1019.0 mb since 10:54 under the ridge. Expect it to fall Sunday into Monday as the trough approaches, though the data doesn't reach that far.

observations.summary: These are Saturday evening readings from 16:35–17:25 local, about 14 h before the first slot. They are current for this run, not for Sunday morning. The south-valley stations already show the drainage: Spanish Fork 151°/11 kt G12, Lehi 144°/10 kt G12, Alpine 161°/6 kt and South Valley Regional 180°/9 kt. Salt Lake airport still has 360°/5 kt but is forecast to turn 150°/6 kt this evening, and Provo is calm. Point of the Mountain and Draper returned no data. The readings agree with the forecast's 140°–160° flow.

d2-am.explanation: The drainage flow is there, but the launch forecast holds it at 140°–150° all morning, under POM South's 160° cut-off for rotor off the hills to the east. Stronger 200°–210° flow (20–22 kt) sits about 5,200 ft up and can mix down once the mixed layer deepens around 11:00. This changes only if the sock settles at 160° or more. The south-valley stations read 151°–180° Saturday evening, so check on site, but don't plan on it.
